title: 5 AI Stocks I Can't Wait to Buy on This Dip
creator: MarketBeat
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; auto-captions garble names/numbers in places
summary: MarketBeat host and guest analyst Thomas Hughes look at five buy-the-dip AI names in the post-midterm sell-off, with the market gripped by fear after Democrats took both houses of Congress and data-centre moratoriums became a live worry. Hughes' core message: selling into peak fear locks in losses; the market is shifting from speculation to execution, and names with accelerating results will lead the next upswing. His rule is to wait for a bottom signal rather than catch a falling knife. AMD is a 'screaming buy' - data-centre revenue up 100% on MI450/Helios, guidance raised five points, growth possibly topping 100% next year, with CPUs gaining as the CPU-to-GPU ratio nears 1:1 for inference. Micron's Taiwan expansion pause is a near-term labour-dispute headwind only; orders are maxed through end of next year into late 2028 and its P/E is under $9. Astera Labs (ALAB), down 50% in a month to below $200 from nearly $500 in June, is the connectivity nuts-and-bolts of AI with accelerating backlog; Hughes reads its chart as an Elliott-wave cycle set to turn. Credo (CRDO), down about 45% in a month, is locked into Nvidia product cycles (copper now, optical next) with rising volume building a support base. Oracle (ORCL) is the most controversial: debt, dilution, spending and cash-flow problems are real, but its backlog tracks toward $1 trillion, capex is set to hit a ceiling and free cash flow should turn positive. All five are CONDITIONAL_BUY - buy only once the market shows a bottom signal.
